name: XBTUSD funding mean reversion (fade extreme funding)
author: BitMEX Research
summary: Funding as a whole shows no predictive power, but extreme funding readings are taken as a counter-trend signal (fade the crowded side).
notes: Original uses 8h XBTUSD funding vs next-period return; mapped to a z-score of the 7-day funding sum. Thresholds and exit-at-mean are our defaults. Page blocks bots; indexed by search.

name: Negative funding spot long
author: Jarvis Labs (jlabsdigital)
summary: Buy spot BTC only when perp funding turns negative (shorts crowded) and sell when funding normalises; claimed +186% over 24 months while deployed fewer than 6 months.
notes: Thread uses aggregated 8h funding; exit level not precise, defaults given (0.0021 = baseline 0.01% x 21 periods).

name: Fear & Greed 20/80 scaling
author: Bitcoin Magazine
summary: Buy 1% of capital each day the index is <= 20 and sell 1% each day it is >= 80; claimed 1,145% vs 1,046% buy-and-hold.
notes: Original scales in/out 1% per day; approximated as a binary position.

name: Buy on second day of Extreme Fear
author: ForkLog
summary: Buy BTC on the second consecutive day of Extreme Fear (index < 25); claimed ~347% over 5 years and ~660% over 6.
notes: Source is accumulation-only (no exit rule); exit on greed is our default.

name: Fear & Greed threshold grid (VectorBT)
author: Code Meets Capital
summary: Grid of buy-below / sell-above Fear & Greed thresholds; very extreme thresholds (10/90) underperform because signals are rare, moderate fear entries do better.
notes: Grid values chosen to bracket the article's tested range; differs from cx-fng-bm-20-80 by including moderate-fear entries.

name: Fear & Greed tiered DCA with greed trimming
author: Reddit user via Cointelegraph
summary: Weekly DCA sized by sentiment ($150 in extreme fear, less as sentiment rises) and sell 5% of holdings weekly in extreme greed; 184% vs 125% plain DCA 2018-2023.
notes: Variable-size DCA accumulation and partial selling cannot be expressed as an on/off position; the binary approximation is cx-fng-bm-20-80.

name: K33 buy at record-low Fear & Greed
author: K33 Research (Vetle Lunde)
summary: Forward returns after the Fear & Greed index hits record-low readings are positive on average and median, though some cases saw continued sell-offs.
notes: K33 studies fixed-horizon forward returns; exit at neutral (50) is our default since the language has no time-based exit.

name: Post-halving peak window (12-18 months)
author: QuantJourney
summary: Cycle tops have come ~373-546 days after halvings; hold from the halving to the end of the peak window, flat in the post-peak bear phase.
notes: Author calls this a template, not a validated strategy; the hold-then-flat mapping is ours. Re-entry happens at the next halving (counter resets).

name: Halving-anchored strategy with MAs and cycle-top indicators
author: FABA journal (UNWE), 2025 no. 2
summary: Combines halving timing with moving averages and cycle-top indicators; beat buy-and-hold in 10 of 13 walk-forward windows with significant alpha.
notes: PDF text could not be extracted (compressed, Bulgarian); exact rules unknown, so left empty. Likely expressible with days_since_halving + sma if the rules are read manually.

name: Bitcoin Monday effect
author: Guglielmo Maria Caporale & Alex Plastun
summary: BTC returns on Mondays are significantly higher than on other weekdays; a strategy holding only Mondays is proposed to exploit it.
notes: Signal at Sunday close holds Monday's bar; exit at Monday close. Later studies (Baur et al.) find the effect not persistent.

name: ETH/BTC ratio above 200-day MA rotation
author: KuCoin
summary: Overweight ETH while the ETH/BTC ratio holds above its 200-day moving average (ETH outperformance cycle), rotate back to BTC when it falls below.
notes: Rotation into BTC when out of ETH is not expressible in a single-asset position; modelled as ETH long/flat. Original also uses fixed ratio levels (0.08/0.10).

name: Taker buy/sell ratio 15d vs 40d MA
author: CryptoQuant analyst via Bitcoinist
summary: Bullish when the 15-day MA of the taker buy/sell ratio rises above 1 while above its 40-day MA.
notes: Buy/sell ratio > 1 is equivalent to taker-buy share > 0.5. Original uses derivatives-exchange taker volume; our taker_ratio may be spot.

name: Binance taker ratio contrarian low
author: CryptoQuant via CryptoPotato
summary: Sharp drops in the Binance futures taker buy/sell ratio to cycle lows (~0.95) have often preceded contrarian bounces.
notes: 'Cycle low' mapped to a new 90-day low of the smoothed ratio; exit when buyers regain majority. Our taker_ratio may be spot, not futures.

name: Taker ratio 30-day MA below 0.98 sell signal
author: CryptoQuant via Comparic
summary: A 30-day MA of the taker buy/sell ratio below ~0.98 marks the strongest sell pressure since 2018 and is read as a sell signal.
notes: 0.98 ratio = 0.4949 taker-buy share. Long condition (ratio > 1) added as the symmetric default. Source in Polish.

name: Hash Ribbons miner capitulation buy
author: Charles Edwards (Capriole)
summary: Buy when the 30-day MA of hash rate crosses back above the 60-day MA after a miner capitulation, confirmed by the 10-day price SMA crossing above the 20-day.
notes: Needs hash rate (on-chain), not in vocabulary.

name: Puell Multiple 0.5 / 4 zones
author: David Puell (metric); CryptoQuant guide
summary: Daily USD miner issuance / its 365-day MA; values under 0.5 are a long signal, over 4 a short signal.
notes: Needs miner issuance data; not in vocabulary.

name: NUPL -0.2 / 0.7 cycle rule
author: CryptoQuant
summary: Net unrealized profit/loss above 0.7 signals proximity to the market top (take profit); -0.2 or lower signals a bottom (accumulate).
notes: Needs realized cap (on-chain).

name: NUPL euphoria (>0.5) phase
author: Glassnode via Cointelegraph
summary: Glassnode marks the classic euphoria phase when NUPL exceeds 0.5 and watches its cooling for local bottoms.
notes: Needs realized cap (on-chain). Threshold differs from CryptoQuant's 0.7 rule.

name: SOPR reset buy (dip to 1 in bull market)
author: Glassnode
summary: In bull markets SOPR dipping to or below 1 (new investors capitulating) and reclaiming it marks buy-the-dip opportunities.
notes: Needs spent-output profit ratio (on-chain).

name: SOPR reset + reset funding buy-the-dip
author: Philip Swift via Cointelegraph
summary: SOPR dropping below 1 combined with reset (neutral/negative) derivatives funding is a strong buy-the-dip signal in a bull market.
notes: The funding half is expressible (funding_7d <= 0) but SOPR is on-chain.

name: SOPR above 1.20 sell signal
author: Ali Martinez (Crypto Briefing)
summary: Each time the 30-day MA of entity-adjusted SOPR rose to ~1.20 or more (2013, 2017) a steep correction followed; treated as a sell signal.
notes: Needs SOPR (on-chain).

name: aSOPR below 1 in bull trend buy / above 1 in bear trend sell
author: CryptoQuant
summary: In bull sentiment, corrections pushing adjusted SOPR below 1 are buy points; in bear sentiment, rallies lifting aSOPR above 1 are sell points.
notes: Needs aSOPR (on-chain).

name: LTH/STH SOPR ratio accumulation
author: CryptoQuant
summary: DCA and hold when the LTH-SOPR / STH-SOPR ratio stays below 1 for extended periods; high ratio marks profit-taking tops.
notes: Needs cohort SOPR (on-chain).

name: Stock-to-flow deviation buy/sell
author: Rekt Capital (PlanB model)
summary: Price deviations far below the S2F model line precede bear-market bottoms (buy) and far above precede bull tops (sell).
notes: Needs the S2F model value (supply/issuance regression); not in vocabulary.

name: PlanB S2F one-standard-deviation band
author: PlanB via Cointelegraph
summary: Price at the low end of the S2F one-stdev band is a buy, top of the band a sell; record -1.5 multiple during FTX.
notes: Needs S2F model; not in vocabulary.

name: MVRV Z-score buy low / sell high (Santiment)
author: Santiment
summary: Accumulate when MVRV z-score is negative (rare, sustained only a few times), take profit at high z-scores.
notes: Needs realized cap (on-chain).

name: MVRV ratio 1 / 3.7 rule
author: CryptoQuant
summary: MVRV above 3.7 = possible market top (sell), below 1 = possible bottom (buy).
notes: Needs realized cap (on-chain).

name: MVRV Z-score red/green band
author: David Puell & Murad Mahmudov (metric)
summary: Z-score of market cap minus realized cap; entering the red zone (~7+) has picked cycle tops within two weeks, the green zone (<0.1) bottoms.
notes: Needs realized cap (on-chain).

name: Pi Cycle Top exit
author: Philip Swift
summary: The 111-day SMA crossing above 2x the 350-day SMA has marked cycle highs to within 3 days; hold otherwise.
notes: Indicator only flags tops; re-entry once the 111DMA drops back below 2x350DMA is our default (may re-enter soon after a top).

name: Mayer Multiple 2.4
author: Trace Mayer
summary: Price / 200-day SMA; historically the best long-run results came from accumulating while the multiple is below 2.4 and avoiding exposure above it.
notes: The 2.4 rule is an accumulation guideline; mapped to long below / flat above. Domain now redirects to bitbo.io's Mayer Multiple chart.

name: Bitcoin 2-Year MA Multiplier (Investor Tool)
author: Philip Swift
summary: Buy when price drops below the 2-year MA, sell when price rises above 5x the 2-year MA.
notes: Direct translation; very few trades. TradingView copy: https://www.tradingview.com/script/0hdOgeox-2-Year-MA-Multiplier/

name: Bull Market Support Band (20W SMA + 21W EMA)
author: Benjamin Cowen (popularised); TradingView script
summary: Price above the 20-week SMA/21-week EMA band = bull regime, below = bear; BTC bull runs ride or bounce off the band.
notes: Weekly MAs approximated with daily lengths x7; weekly-close confirmation not expressible.

name: Perpetual futures no-arbitrage deviation trade
author: Songrun He, Asaf Manela, Omri Ross, Victor von Wachter
summary: Trade the gap between perp price and its no-arbitrage value implied by funding; claimed large Sharpe ratios after Binance costs.
notes: Market-neutral spot-perp arbitrage; needs perp vs spot prices and two legs.

name: Funding-rate cash-and-carry (long spot, short perp)
author: 1Token
summary: Hold spot and short the perpetual to collect positive funding delta-neutrally.
notes: Two-leg hedged carry; the single-asset position model cannot express it.

name: CME futures basis cash-and-carry
author: Sharpe AI
summary: Long spot BTC / short CME future to lock the annualised basis (3-8% in bear markets, 10-25% in bull runs).
notes: Needs futures curve data and a hedged two-leg position.

name: CME gap fill
author: TradingView community
summary: Weekend gaps between the CME Friday close and Sunday open tend to fill (claimed 65-95%), so trade toward the gap.
notes: Needs CME futures session prices; 24/7 spot daily bars have no weekend gap.

name: Coinbase premium index signal
author: CryptoQuant
summary: High/increasing Coinbase-vs-Binance premium = US institutional accumulation (bullish); low/decreasing = whale selling (bearish).
notes: Needs exchange-specific prices.

name: Korea (kimchi) premium above 16% top signal
author: CryptoQuant
summary: Korean exchange premium over ~16% historically indicated a local top / retail FOMO.
notes: Needs Korean exchange prices and KRW FX.

name: GBTC premium/discount sentiment
author: CryptoQuant
summary: High GBTC premium = US bullishness and downside risk; low premium / discount = bearish sentiment and upside potential (contrarian).
notes: Needs GBTC price and NAV.

name: Crypto time-series momentum (Liu & Tsyvinski)
author: Yukun Liu & Aleh Tsyvinski
summary: Strong time-series momentum: past one- to several-week BTC returns predict next-week returns.
notes: Paper uses weekly returns and regressions; daily rebalancing on a rolling n-day return is our approximation. Published RFS 2021.

name: Investor attention (Google searches) predicts crypto returns
author: Yukun Liu & Aleh Tsyvinski
summary: Abnormal Google search and Twitter counts for bitcoin forecast future returns.
notes: Needs Google Trends / Twitter data.

name: Tether issuance after downturns
author: John Griffin & Amin Shams
summary: Tether-funded purchases timed after BTC downturns produced sizable price increases; new USDT issuance as a bullish flow signal.
notes: Needs stablecoin issuance/flow data. Published J. Finance 2020.

name: Stablecoin Supply Ratio buying power
author: Glassnode
summary: Low SSR (BTC cap / stablecoin cap) = high stablecoin buying power (bullish); high SSR = bearish.
notes: Needs stablecoin supply; not in vocabulary.

name: SSR oscillator (SSR / 200d SMA with 2-sd bands)
author: Footprint Analytics
summary: Normalise SSR by its 200-day SMA with Bollinger-style 2-sd bands; lower-band breaches flag oversold buy zones, upper-band overbought.
notes: Needs stablecoin supply.

name: Exchange reserve trend
author: CryptoQuant
summary: Rising BTC exchange reserves = accumulating sell pressure (bearish); falling reserves = low sell pressure (bullish).
notes: Needs exchange balances (on-chain).

name: Exchange netflow accumulation signal
author: Axel Adler Jr.
summary: Net BTC inflows to exchanges = coming sell pressure (bearish); sustained net outflows = accumulation (bullish).
notes: Needs exchange flow data (on-chain).

name: BTC outflow + stablecoin inflow breakout entry
author: Jarvis Labs
summary: Go long into resistance when the 30-day MA of BTC exchange netflow is negative and stablecoin exchange inflows rise; close longs when BTC netflow turns positive and stablecoin flows turn negative.
notes: Needs BTC and stablecoin exchange flows.

name: USDC exchange netflow buy signal
author: Labs DA
summary: Three conditions on CryptoQuant USDC (ERC20) exchange netflow, backtested in TradingView, preceded BTC rallies.
notes: Needs stablecoin exchange flow data.

name: Crowded long/short ratio fade
author: K33 Research
summary: A long/short account ratio above ~3 signals over-confident longs and foreshadows selling pressure; ratios near 1 are a weak signal.
notes: Needs exchange long/short account data and open interest.

name: Open interest vs price divergence (liquidation cascade setup)
author: Axel Adler Jr.
summary: Rising open interest while price falls loads a long-liquidation cascade; negative funding with rising short OI is a contrarian long setup.
notes: Needs open interest; the funding-only part is covered by cx-negative-funding-spot-long.

name: Short squeeze from crowded short OI
author: Jarvis Labs
summary: Short OI building into rallies and CME backwardation mark crowded shorts that get squeezed; price rising with falling OI is a healthy unwind; buy the liquidation cascade retest of the 200-day MA.
notes: Needs open interest, liquidations and CME term structure.

name: Estimated leverage ratio risk gauge
author: CryptoQuant
summary: Open interest / exchange reserve; high or sharply rising ELR = over-leveraged, crowded market prone to liquidation volatility (de-risk).
notes: Needs open interest and exchange reserves.

name: NVT Signal dynamic range
author: Willy Woo / Dmitry Kalichkin (metric)
summary: Market cap / 90-day MA of on-chain transaction volume, with 2-year MA +/- stdev bands flagging over/undervaluation.
notes: Needs on-chain transaction volume.

name: NVT Golden Cross -1.6 / 2.2
author: CryptoQuant
summary: Bollinger-like comparison of short- vs long-term NVT trend; above 2.2 = short signal, below -1.6 = long signal.
notes: Needs on-chain transaction volume.

name: NVM ratio RSI 30/70
author: CryptoQuant
summary: RSI of the network-value-to-Metcalfe ratio with 70/30 thresholds spots local tops and bottoms.
notes: Needs active addresses.

name: RHODL ratio cycle top
author: Philip Swift
summary: Ratio of the 1-week to 1-2yr realized HODL bands; entering the red band signals an overheated market and a profit-taking point.
notes: Needs realized HODL waves (on-chain).

name: Golden Ratio Multiplier (350DMA x 1.6/2/3)
author: Philip Swift
summary: Multiples of the 350-day MA (1.6, 2, 3, 5, 8...) act as resistance at intracycle and cycle highs; smart investors manage risk at those bands.
notes: Page gives only the sell/risk bands; buying back below the 350DMA (or 1.6x) is our default. Author notes the multiples may shrink as adoption matures.

name: 200-week MA heatmap
author: PlanB (@100trillionUSD), modified by LookIntoBitcoin
summary: BTC has bottomed near the 200-week MA each cycle (buy near it); orange/red months when the 200WMA's monthly % increase is high mark overheating (sell).
notes: Colour thresholds are not published; thr is our guess for the red band. 200 weeks = 1400 daily bars; needs long history.

name: Altcoin Season Index (ETH proxy)
author: Blockchaincenter.net
summary: Altcoin season when 75% of the top 50 coins outperform BTC over 90 days (index >= 75); Bitcoin season when <= 25.
notes: Breadth of top-50 alts is not available; ETH vs BTC 90-day relative performance is used as a one-asset proxy. Original is a regime gauge, not a trading rule.

name: Bitcoin MAX (buy x-day high) strategy
author: Sona Beluska / Quantpedia (after Padysak & Vojtko 2022)
summary: Hold BTC for the next day whenever the price sits at its 10-50 day maximum; stayed effective out of sample 2022-2024 with lower drawdowns than buy-and-hold.
notes: Original uses daily open prices at 00:00 UTC and one-day holding; equivalent to being long only on days after a new n-day high.

name: Bitcoin MIN (buy x-day low) strategy
author: Sona Beluska / Quantpedia (after Padysak & Vojtko 2022)
summary: Hold BTC for the next day whenever the price sits at its 10-50 day minimum; worked in-sample but performed poorly out of sample (2022-2024).
notes: Original uses daily open prices and one-day holding.

name: Bitcoin 21:00-23:00 UTC intraday seasonality
author: Quantpedia
summary: Holding BTC only from 21:00 to 23:00 UTC gave ~40.6% annualised with -22.7% max drawdown; stronger on uptrend and high-volatility days.
notes: Intraday hourly strategy; cannot be expressed on daily bars.

name: Skip September (worst BTC month)
author: Cointelegraph
summary: September has delivered BTC's lowest average monthly return (~-3% over 13 years); be flat in September, long otherwise.
notes: Assumes days_to_month_end == 0 on the last day of the month so the position is flat for all September bars. The article reports seasonality, not a tested rule.

name: Q4 'Uptober' seasonal long
author: Cointelegraph / Mikybull Crypto
summary: October-December is BTC's best quarter (~78% average gain); hold only in Q4.
notes: Assumes days_to_month_end == 0 on the last day of the month. The analyst's 'green September implies Q4 rally' filter is not included.

name: Taker buy/sell ratio above 1
author: CryptoQuant
summary: Taker buy/sell volume ratio above 1 = aggressive buyers dominate (bullish); below 1 = sellers dominate (bearish).
notes: Ratio > 1 equals taker-buy share > 0.5. Guide describes perpetual swaps; our taker_ratio may be spot. Smoothing window is our choice.

name: Mayer Multiple risk bands (Glassnode)
author: Glassnode
summary: Mayer Multiple above +2 standard deviations = very high risk; below 1 = low risk; used as the price-only leg of a cycle risk framework.
notes: Glassnode combines it with MVRV > 1 (on-chain, dropped). Std window not stated; n is our choice.

name: Exchange volume momentum (30D vs 365D) risk
author: Glassnode
summary: 30-day MA of exchange volume above its 365-day MA and rising = very high risk; below and falling = very low risk.
notes: Risk gauge turned into accumulate-in-low-risk / exit-in-very-high-risk; our volume is one venue's USD turnover rather than all exchanges.

name: Global liquidity expansion regime
author: LookIntoBitcoin
summary: Bitcoin bull markets have coincided with rapid expansion of global liquidity (M2 of 8 central banks plus Fed liabilities and reverse repo).
notes: Our netliq is a US Fed net-liquidity series, not global M2; the page claims coincidence, not a timing rule. Trend filter is our default.

name: Fear & Greed positive-sentiment trend
author: Huang, Xu, Xue & Zhang (Corporate Ownership & Control)
summary: ARDL on 2016-2021 monthly data finds a positive, significant long-run link from the Fear & Greed index to BTC returns (sentiment follows through rather than reverting).
notes: Paper is an econometric study, not a trading rule; long-when-greedy is the direct reading of its sign. Page blocks bots (403).

name: DXY below its moving averages = BTC tailwind
author: Jarvis Labs
summary: DXY and BTC are inversely correlated; DXY losing its moving averages supports BTC strength and a DXY backtest of lost MAs pressures BTC.
notes: Article is discretionary commentary; MA lengths are our defaults.

name: Glassnode Bitcoin Sharpe Signal (long)
author: Glassnode
summary: Machine-learned on-chain signal; going long BTC when it rises above 0.5 has historically improved risk-adjusted performance (data since 2012).
notes: Proprietary model on on-chain inputs.

name: Glassnode Bitcoin Sharpe Signal Short
author: Glassnode
summary: ML model that flags high-confidence downturns (indicator > 0.5); captured the 2022 bear out of sample without false signals in 2023-24.
notes: Proprietary model.

name: STH-SOPR below 1 local-bottom entry
author: Glassnode
summary: Short-term-holder SOPR dipping just below 1 has marked local bottoms and good entry points.
notes: Needs cohort SOPR (on-chain).

name: LTH-SOPR above 10 cycle top
author: Glassnode
summary: Long-term-holder SOPR values above 10 have marked cycle tops; LTH capitulation (red zones) coincides with major bottoms.
notes: Needs cohort SOPR (on-chain).

name: Short-term holder realized price bull/bear line
author: LookIntoBitcoin (Glassnode STH-MVRV concept)
summary: Price above the STH cost basis (STH-MVRV > 1) = bull regime, below = bear; breaking the line has signalled reversals before classic MVRV.
notes: Needs UTXO-age cost basis (on-chain).

name: Price below realized price accumulation
author: LookIntoBitcoin
summary: Price falling below the aggregate on-chain cost basis has coincided with major cycle lows; moving back above starts bull phases.
notes: Needs realized cap (on-chain).

name: Finding floors: 0.7x realized price vs 0.6x 200D SMA
author: Glassnode
summary: Intersection of 0.7x realized price and 0.6x 200-day SMA marks the deepest bear-market phase (one of ten recovery indicators, with others like 30D/365D new-address and 90D/365D fee crossovers).
notes: Realized price is on-chain; the 200D SMA leg alone is expressible.

name: Cost-basis distribution capitulation / local-top metrics
author: Glassnode
summary: Loss-weighted selling spikes (7-day EMA) align with major bottoms, profit-weighted spikes with major tops.
notes: Needs on-chain cost-basis distribution.

name: STH capitulation z-scores (local bottoms in a bull market)
author: Glassnode
summary: Negative z-scores of STH MVRV and SOPR by age band, confirmed by high STH realized losses propagating from 1-day to longer bands, mark bull-market local bottoms.
notes: Needs cohort on-chain data.

name: Leverage position openings/closures (price x OI trend)
author: Glassnode
summary: Classify price/OI trend combos; elevated long closures after drops mark local bottoms, sharp ramps in long openings precede tops, short openings then closures precede squeezes.
notes: Needs open interest.

name: Options skew index confirmation/divergence
author: Glassnode
summary: UpVol minus DownVol across tenors: rising skew with rising spot confirms; rallies with sharply negative skew are distrusted; negative 1w with positive 3-6m skew = temporary stress.
notes: Needs options implied volatility surface.

name: ETF flows vs miner issuance around the halving
author: Glassnode
summary: Compare spot-ETF purchases with post-halving miner issuance (~450 BTC/day) and the LTH market inflation rate; slowing ETF inflows before the halving warn of a sell-the-news correction.
notes: Needs ETF flow and LTH supply data.

name: Bitcoin Rainbow Chart bands
author: azop / trolololo / Blockchaincenter
summary: Log-regression of price vs time with colour bands; lower bands = buy, top red band = maximum bubble / sell.
notes: Needs regression on time since genesis (y = 2.9065 ln(x) - 19.493); no time/log functions in the vocabulary.

name: Bitcoin power-law corridor
author: LookIntoBitcoin (Giovanni Santostasi model)
summary: Price follows a power law in time; price stretched to the upper bound is overbought, near the lower bound oversold.
notes: Needs log-log regression on time since genesis.

name: Top Cap (35x average cap)
author: Willy Woo (@woonomic)
summary: 35x the all-history average market cap has flagged parabolic cycle tops (missed the rounded 2021 top).
notes: Price-only, but needs an expanding mean since 2009 (no cumulative function in the vocabulary).

name: Delta Top (7x delta cap)
author: Willy Woo / David Puell (Delta Cap)
summary: Delta cap (realized cap minus average cap) x7 flags the very tops of BTC cycles.
notes: Needs realized cap.

name: CVDD bottom floor
author: Willy Woo (@woonomic)
summary: Cumulative value coin-days-destroyed / market age x 6M has forecast BTC's major lows; price touching CVDD is a bottom zone.
notes: Needs coin days destroyed (on-chain).

name: Terminal Price cycle top
author: Checkmate (@_checkmatey_)
summary: Transferred price (CDD / supply / age) x 21 has anticipated cycle tops.
notes: Needs coin days destroyed.

name: Reserve Risk green/red zones
author: Hans Hauge (Ikigai Asset Management)
summary: Price / HODL Bank (holders' accumulated opportunity cost); green zone = high confidence + low price (buy), red zone = sell.
notes: Needs coin days destroyed.

name: Value Days Destroyed multiple +2.9
author: TXMC (@TXMCtrades)
summary: 30d/365d ratio of value days destroyed; readings above 2.9 (top 5% of history) align with cycle highs.
notes: Needs coin days destroyed.

name: 1yr+ HODL wave distribution top
author: LookIntoBitcoin (Unchained Capital HODL waves)
summary: The share of supply unmoved for 1yr+ falls as long-term holders sell into rising prices; mass LTH movement signals major highs.
notes: Needs UTXO age data.

name: Active Address Sentiment Indicator
author: LookIntoBitcoin
summary: 28-day % change of price vs 28-day % change of active addresses with stdev bands; price change at upper band = overheated (sell), at lower band = oversold (buy).
notes: Needs active address counts.

name: Exchange inflow CDD spike sell signal
author: CryptoQuant
summary: High coin-days-destroyed flowing into exchanges means long-held coins are being readied for sale: possible sell pressure or trend reversal.
notes: Needs on-chain exchange flows.

name: Miners' Position Index exit timing
author: CryptoQuant
summary: Miner outflows in USD / 365-day MA; high or rising MPI = miners selling (bearish), used to time exits by copying miners.
notes: Needs miner outflow data.

name: Miner-to-exchange flow
author: CryptoQuant
summary: High or increasing BTC flow from mining pools to exchanges = miners preparing to sell (bearish); low/decreasing = bullish.
notes: Needs on-chain miner flows.

name: Binary CDD long-term holder spending
author: CryptoQuant
summary: High density of 1s (CDD above average) = LTHs moving coins for possible selling; bar-code patterns typify bear markets.
notes: Needs coin days destroyed.

name: Exchange BTC/stablecoin reserve ratio
author: CryptoQuant
summary: BTC reserves divided by stablecoin reserves held on exchanges; high values indicate potential sell pressure.
notes: Needs exchange reserves.

name: Google Trends / Wikipedia attention feedback
author: Ladislav Kristoufek
summary: Search interest and BTC price are strongly linked both ways; rising interest amplifies moves in the direction of the price trend (bubble feedback).
notes: Needs Google Trends / Wikipedia views.

name: Post-halving sell-the-news pause
author: Glassnode Finance Bridge
summary: The 2016, 2020 and 2024 halvings were each followed by an immediate correction (BTC -16% in the weeks after April 2024); stand aside right after the halving, hold otherwise.
notes: Article describes the pattern without a rule; window length is our default.

name: Positive funding persists in bull markets
author: CryptoQuant
summary: Positive funding reflects longs in control and tends to persist in bull markets; high funding does not by itself predict a drop, so follow the funding sign.
notes: Guide is interpretive, not a backtested rule; trend-following reading of the funding sign (opposite of cx-negative-funding-spot-long).
